newsitem.title: USA: Stocks extend strong gains; Dow jumps 60 points.
newsitem.headline: Stocks extend strong gains; Dow jumps 60 points.

text.p: Stocks romped ahead for a third day Wednesday as investors shook off the inflationary implications in a report that showed robust economic growth and lifted the Dow Jones industrial average within striking range of its record high.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow was up 60.61 points at 7,022.64 after Tuesday's gain of 179 points -- its second largest ever -- positioned the blue chip index for an assault on its March 11 record close of 7,085.16.
In the broader market, advancing issues outnumbered declines 2-1 on heavy volume of 311 million the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 17.33 points to 1,259.96.
"I'm seeing people buying stocks at all costs," said Doug Myers, vice president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane.
Analysts said a turnaround in the bond market helped to ignite a fresh buying spree in stocks.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond gained 18/32, sending its yield down to 6.94 percent from Tuesday's close of 6.98 percent. The bond's price and yield move in opposite directions.
Both stocks and bonds traded lower in early morning after a report on the economy renewed interest-rate worries.
The Commerce Department reported the nation's gross domestic product expanded at a 5.6 percent annual rate in the first three months of this year, its fastest pace in more than nine years.
The GDP number was much stronger than Wall Street economists' forecasts for a 4.1 percent rate of growth.
But some analysts said the GDP data were skewed by accumulation of inventories, which will reduce growth in the second quarter.
"The GDP figure has some bad news and some confirmation of the good news that we had yesterday," said Stanley Nabi, vice chairman at Wood Struthers & Winthrop.

Stocks rallied Tuesday on economic data, including the first quarter employment cost index, that hinted at moderate inflation pressure in wages, which fuelled specalation that the Federal Reserve may hold interest rates steady at its policy-setting meeting on May 20.
Technical analysts said that if stocks were to continue rallying, it would be important for the market to reach new highs, although not necessarily on Wednesday.
A significant market retreat before new highs are set would be a sign of a faltering market, they said.
"If this is going to be a resumption of the rally attempt, and it's looking like it so far today, to get a new high is a critical piece of the puzzle," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at Everen.
Among individual stocks, Estee Lauder Cos. rose 1 to 46 after Prudential Securities upgraded the stock.
Boston Scientific Corp., hammered earlier this month after an earnings warning, rallied 6-3/8 to 48-7/8 on better-than-expected quarterly earnings.
Bank and technology stocks added to their recent gains.
Citicorp rose 2-5/8 to 114-5/8, Chase Manhattan Corp. rose 2-1/8 to 92-5/8. International Business Machines Corp. was up 1-3/8 to 159-3/4 and Hewlett-Packard Co. tacked on 2-1/8 to 53-3/4.
